diagnosis: I calibrated the model with three DDS runs (6,500 model runs in total) on the full 1971–1997 period, optimising NSE. Daily NSE is 0.768, KGE 0.70 and r 0.88. The model still overestimates flow by about 18% (PBIAS). Observed runoff is only about 0.97 mm/d against 2.32 mm/d precipitation and 1.35 mm/d PET. That means evaporation would have to equal PET for the water to balance, which suggests water leaves the catchment underground, probably through the chalk and sand aquifers. HBV has no term for such losses. The optimiser compensated through high soil storage and evaporation (FC about 340 mm, LP about 0.7) and by discarding snowfall (SFCF at its lower bound of 0.4, with TT about -2 °C). Snow is only about 1% of precipitation, so the snow parameters have little effect and should not be read as physical. The likely weak points are low summer flows (too high, because of the bias) and some flood peaks. Response parameters (K1 0.33, K2 0.06, PERC 1.9, MAXBAS 2.1) were stable across the three runs, and NSE levelled off at about 0.768, so I'm moderately confident in them. I did not test on a separate period, so I can't say how well this will hold up in 1998–2008. With a similar climate I'd expect NSE of roughly 0.7–0.77.
